{"id":"vouch-xlha.12","title":"attest: non-ASCII SSH key text crashes with a traceback","description":"git-vouch-attest:143-146 (parse_sk_key) catches only binascii.Error around base64.b64decode(fields[1], validate=True). When given a str containing a non-ASCII character, b64decode raises a plain ValueError ("string argument should contain only ASCII characters"), which is not a binascii.Error. Nothing up the stack catches it: main() at 409-415 catches only AttestError and OSError.

Reproduced:
- File mode: a .pub whose base64 field contains 0xc3 0xa9 is decoded with "replace" at line 403 to U+FFFD, and the tool exits 1 with a full Python traceback.
- Person-file mode: {"keys":[{"ssh":"sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com AAAAé", "attestation":{...}}]} gives the same traceback. Every later key in the file is then left unverified and unreported, because the exception escapes the per-key loop at 408-413.

The tool fails closed (exit 1), but person files are attacker-authored input. One malformed key hides the verdicts for the rest, and users will file the traceback as a bug.

Fix: catch ValueError there; binascii.Error is a subclass, so `except ValueError` covers both. Add a test with a non-ASCII key in a person file next to a valid attested key, and assert that the valid key still prints "verified".
